chapters.text: Nora turns her glass slowly. "My Jim pulled pints in this very bar in 1971. He used to say you can tell everything about a barman from his stout."
chapters.ask_text: Pour Nora a stout that scores 90 or more

chapters.text: "That was Jim's pint. I haven't tasted one like it in forty years." She slides an old photograph across the bar: the pub in 1971, Jim grinning behind the taps. "Put it on the wall. It belongs here."
Packie taps the bar. "Thirty years I've held the title in this parish. Not beaten since '94. Do you throw a dart yourself, or are you all talk like the rest of them?"
chapters.ask_text: Give Packie a game of darts (you'll need the dartboard)

chapters.text: "Fair play, you gave me a game." He lowers his voice. "The parish league needs a home venue. I told them this was the only place. They'll be in, and they're thirsty men."
Tomás rests his fiddle case on the stool beside him. "I've tunes in me and nowhere to play them. Give me a corner and I'd bring the lads."
chapters.ask_text: Build the snug corner stage for Tomás

chapters.text: "A stage! Now book us in some night. A fiddle by the fire on a quiet Tuesday, that's all it takes to fill a room."
chapters.ask_text: Book a live music night (Menu, Live music)

chapters.text: "I hear you've a drum behind the bar. Sit in with us some night. You'd keep better time than Declan, God love him."
chapters.ask_text: Sit in on the bodhrán during a live session

chapters.text: Liam is drawing plays on a beer mat. "My under-12s are in the county final. If we win I'll bring the whole team and the parents in for minerals. Have you a soda gun at all?"
chapters.ask_text: Put in a soda gun for the under-12s

chapters.text: Liam bursts in, hoarse. "WE WON! Two points in injury time! The lads are outside. Lemonades all round, and I'll have a pint myself."
"A pub's not a pub without a table quiz," Margaret announces. "I'd run one myself, if there was a drop of Ballyfinn behind the bar for the quizmaster."
chapters.ask_text: Put in the whiskey optic for Margaret

chapters.text: "The quiz was a triumph. The Kilbrack crowd were robbed on the tie-break, of course." She presses an envelope into your hand. "Your share of the raffle. Same time next month."
Eamon sniffs his pint. "There's a taste of the pipes off that. When did you last clean them lines? My father could tell a dirty line from the far end of the bar."
chapters.ask_text: Clean the beer lines in the cellar

chapters.text: "Now that's a pint." He nods slowly, which from Eamon is a standing ovation. "I'll tell the lads at the mart."
Aoife sinks onto a stool, still in her scrubs. "Twelve hours on the ward. What I'd give for a cold cider on draught. Bottles just aren't the same."
chapters.ask_text: Put the cider tap on for Aoife

chapters.text: "You're a saint." She raises the glass. "The whole night shift will be in after this, you know. Nurses drink like fish."
